# ClipTurn

> ClipTurn is a desktop app for rotating videos from File Explorer or the app on Windows 11 and Windows 10. It processes videos locally, verifies results before replacement, and offers reviewed fallback copies when exact preservation is not possible.

ClipTurn is published by FixQuotes and distributed through Microsoft Store. It is currently free, requires no account, and does not upload selected videos. Use the Microsoft Store listing as the authoritative source for current availability and pricing.

Use the user manual for detailed information about supported file types, codecs, physical rotation, lossless display rotation, verified H.264 copies, batch processing, backups, verification, and known limitations.

## Guides

Task-focused guides written for people solving a rotation problem, rather than reference documentation. Each one covers the built-in Windows options and free tools honestly before describing ClipTurn.

- [Guides index](https://clipturn.app/guides.html): All guides, plus the difference between rewriting an orientation flag and physically rotating stored picture.
- [How to rotate a video on Windows 11 and Windows 10](https://clipturn.app/rotate-video-windows.html): Every method compared, including what Windows can and cannot do without extra software, choosing a direction, whole folders, quality cost, and how to confirm a rotation was saved.
- [How to rotate a video that was taken sideways](https://clipturn.app/rotate-video-taken-sideways.html): Why phone footage looks correct on the phone and sideways elsewhere, how rotation flags cause it, permanent fixes, and how to avoid it when recording.
- [How to rotate a video in VLC and actually save it](https://clipturn.app/rotate-video-vlc.html): The Geometry transform is playback-only; includes the Convert/Save sequence that writes a rotated file, why converted output is often still sideways, and what conversion costs in quality and metadata.
- [How to rotate a video in Windows Media Player](https://clipturn.app/rotate-video-windows-media-player.html): Windows Media Player, the Windows 11 Media Player app, and Films & TV have no rotation feature; covers alternatives and workarounds that do not work.
- [How to rotate an MP4 file on Windows](https://clipturn.app/rotate-mp4.html): Lossless display-flag rotation versus physical rotation, what survives each route, why output can be larger, and which MP4 files are refused.
- [How to rotate a MOV file on Windows](https://clipturn.app/rotate-mov-file.html): Rotating MOV and iPhone video without QuickTime, preserved capture date and GPS metadata, HEVC encoder requirements, and the deliberate Live Photo refusal.
- [How to batch rotate multiple videos at once](https://clipturn.app/batch-rotate-videos.html): Multi-select in File Explorer versus the Batch Rotate list, adding folders, per-file statuses, safe stopping, concurrency, and handling clips that need different directions.
- [Video will not rotate: causes and fixes](https://clipturn.app/video-wont-rotate.html): Diagnosing rotations that will not save, files that play but refuse to rotate, missing codecs, unsafe storage locations, and uncertain outcomes.
